title: Profiling of antibody responses to human norovirus in animals

analysis.research_question_and_background: Noroviruses are a major cause of acute gastroenteritis globally, with over 30 genotypes circulating in humans, some widespread, and others sporadically detected. analysis.methods: Using a multiplex protein microarray spanning 30 norovirus genotypes, we profiled antibody responses in sera from 17 animal species. Binding-blocking assays performed on selected sera confirmed some of the detected antibody responses.
analysis.main_results: High antibody titers to multiple antigens were observed in sera from cats, dogs, and several duck species, and chickens, whereas lower titers to fewer genotypes were observed in sera from rats, pigs, horses, and wild boar. analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The strong and broadly reactive antibody profiles observed in cats, dogs, and birds warrant further investigation to determine whether these responses indicate true circulation of human noroviruses or are due to cross-reactivity. analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report clear evidence of human norovirus circulation in animals, and the study design does not include direct viral detection methods. Some responses were confirmed by binding-blocking assays, but the study found no clear evidence of human norovirus circulation in animals. The results suggest that most antibody responses may reflect cross-reactivity rather than true circulation. These findings highlight the need for further investigation into the potential role of animals in human norovirus transmission and may inform surveillance and risk assessment strategies.

title: Clinical complications during hospitalizations of all-cause and norovirus acute gastroenteritis among adults in the United States, 2022–2024

analysis.research_question_and_background: Norovirus is the leading cause of acute gastroenteritis (AGE) globally, but contemporary data on clinical complications during hospitalizations for all-cause and norovirus-associated AGE are limited. This study aimed to characterize clinical complications during acute hospitalizations among adults with all-cause and norovirus AGE.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A descriptive study was conducted using Optum’s de-identified Clinformatics ® Data Mart (Optum® CDM) administrative claims database. Adults aged ≥ 18 years with hospitalized all-cause AGE or norovirus-specified episodes between July 2022 and June 2024 were identified using ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes.
analysis.methods: Baseline frailty among adults aged ≥ 60 years was assessed using a validated claims-based frailty index. Clinical complications during acute hospitalizations occurring within 3 days of the index episode were evaluated by age group (18–59 and ≥ 60 years) and presence of underlying medical conditions.
analysis.main_results: The study included 192,430 hospitalized all-cause AGE episodes and 2,589 hospitalized norovirus-coded episodes. Metabolic disturbances, acute kidney injury, dehydration, and sepsis were the most common complications among patients with all-cause AGE (57.2%, 38.3%, 29.2%, and 26.5%, respectively) or norovirus-coded episodes (62.0%, 42.6%, 41.9%, and 28.1%, respectively).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that hospitalized adults with all-cause and norovirus-coded AGE commonly experienced renal, metabolic, and systemic complications. These findings improve the clinical characterization of severe AGE, specifically norovirus, and identify populations at greatest risk for adverse outcomes.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform targeted surveillance and risk assessment for severe AGE, particularly among adults with norovirus infection, and highlight the need for improved clinical management and prevention strategies in high-risk groups.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on administrative claims data, which may introduce bias and lack detailed clinical information. The evidence is moderate as it provides descriptive insights into complications but does not establish causal relationships.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to characterize clinical complications during hospitalizations for all-cause and norovirus-associated acute gastroenteritis (AGE) among adults in the United States from 2022 to 2024. Using Optum’s administrative claims database, researchers identified 192,430 all-cause AGE episodes and 2,589 norovirus-coded episodes. They found that metabolic disturbances, acute kidney injury, dehydration, and sepsis were the most common complications, with high frequencies observed in both older and younger adults. The study highlights the need for improved clinical management and prevention strategies for severe AGE, particularly among adults with norovirus infection. However, the reliance on administrative data introduces potential biases, limiting the strength of the evidence to moderate.

title: HIRSCHSPRUNG DISEASE: WHEN BOWEL DYSFUNCTION TAKES A SYSTEMIC TURN - A CASE REPORT

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hirschsprung disease (HD) is a rare congenital disorder of the enteric nervous system, caused by impaired neural crest cell migration during intestinal development. This leads to aganglionosis of the distal bowel, most frequently affecting the rectosigmoid colon.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a case report describing a 4-year-old boy with a history of HD treated two years prior with a Swenson pull-through procedure. He presented to the paediatric emergency department with a one-day history of abdominal pain, fetid diarrhoea, and vomiting. No other symptoms were recorded.
analysis.methods: Oral antiemetics and hydration were administered. During hospitalization, he remained lethargic with progressive abdominal distension, for which intravenous fluids were initiated for maintenance and replacement of ongoing losses. Initial laboratory tests and blood cultures were unremarkable. Gastrointestinal molecular panel was positive for norovirus, with a negative stool culture. Gastrointestinal decompression was performed via nasogastric tube placement, with drainage of faecal material, and rectal enema, with explosive discharge of stools.
analysis.main_results: Abdominal radiography showed marked dilatation of bowel loops and faecal loading. Laboratory reassessment showed severe metabolic acidosis (pH and HCO3 below the measurable range), hyperlactatemia (9.8 mmol/L), acute kidney injury (creatinine 0.9 mg/dL; 2.25-fold increase from baseline), and elevated inflammatory markers (C-reactive protein 27.7 mg/dL and procalcitonin >100 ng/mL), findings consistent with severe HAEC presenting with mixed hypovolemic/septic shock. Gastric residual progressively decreased, alongside marked improvement in abdominal distension. The patient was discharged after 12 days, clinically and analytically stable, with normalization of renal function.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: HAEC is a complication which may happen both before and after surgery, in 20-40% of HD patients. During the initial stages, clinical presentation is non-specific and can mimic acute gastroenteritis. However, patients may rapidly progress to mixed hypovolemic/distributive (septic) shock. Management relies on aggressive fluid therapy for haemodynamic stabilization and gastrointestinal source control. Broad-spectrum antibiotics are mandatory for seven to ten days, with coverage of anaerobes and enteric gram-negative organisms. Gastrointestinal decompression is crucial, with nasogastric tube placement, serial rectal irrigations, and bowel rest.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: A high index of clinical suspicion is required for timely diagnosis and management. The findings highlight the importance of recognizing HAEC as a potential complication in HD patients, even after surgical intervention, and emphasize the need for prompt and aggressive treatment strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report limitations. The evidence is based on a single case report, which provides limited generalizability. However, the findings are consistent with known clinical manifestations of HAEC and norovirus infection, supporting a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes a 4-year-old boy with Hirschsprung disease who developed Hirschsprung-associated Enterocolitis (HAEC) two years after undergoing a Swenson pull-through procedure. The patient presented with abdominal pain, fetid diarrhoea, and vomiting, and was found to have norovirus infection. Despite initial non-specific symptoms, he rapidly deteriorated with signs of severe HAEC, including metabolic acidosis, acute kidney injury, and septic shock. Aggressive fluid therapy, antibiotics, and gastrointestinal decompression were initiated, leading to clinical and analytical stability after 12 days. The case underscores the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion for HAEC in HD patients, even post-surgery, and highlights the potential role of norovirus in triggering such complications. The evidence is based on a single case report, which provides moderate confidence due to its limited generalizability.

title: Eculizumab Therapy in Suspected Late-Onset Atypical Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome in an Adult Kidney Transplant Recipient: A Case Report

analysis.research_question_and_background: Atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (aHUS) is a rare, life-threatening, complement-mediated thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA) that may occur de novo after kidney transplantation.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Because its manifestations overlap with more common causes of allograft dysfunction, including rejection, calcineurin inhibitor toxicity, and infection, diagnosis can be challenging.
analysis.methods: The disease may progress rapidly, making early clinical suspicion and timely etiologic evaluation essential.
analysis.main_results: His serum creatinine had remained approximately 2.0 mg/dL after treatment for suspected chronic active antibody-mediated rejection but increased to 6.57 mg/dL at outpatient follow-up and to 8.47 mg/dL on admission after a recent norovirus infection.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Elevated lactate dehydrogenase, decreased haptoglobin, fragmented red blood cells, and allograft biopsy findings supported TMA.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This case highlights the importance of considering TMA when graft dysfunction progresses rapidly or remains unexplained, even many years after kidney transplantation.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Early recognition of microangiopathic features and prompt evaluation for the underlying etiology are particularly important when complement-mediated aHUS is suspected, because established acute-on-chronic allograft injury may limit renal recovery despite hematologic response to C5 inhibition.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes a 52-year-old man who developed abrupt, severe graft dysfunction 10 years after ABO-incompatible kidney transplantation. His serum creatinine levels rose to 8.47 mg/dL following a recent norovirus infection, prompting suspicion of thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA). Initial evaluations considered common post-transplant causes of graft dysfunction, but as renal dysfunction progressed and hematologic abnormalities emerged, TMA was suspected. Laboratory findings, including elevated lactate dehydrogenase, decreased haptoglobin, and fragmented red blood cells, supported the TMA diagnosis. Genetic testing identified a heterozygous CFH variant, but no HLA antibodies or Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli were detected. Eculizumab was initiated, leading to resolution of hematologic abnormalities, but renal function did not recover. The case underscores the importance of considering TMA in unexplained graft dysfunction, particularly when complement-mediated aHUS is suspected, as acute-on-chronic injury may hinder recovery despite hematologic improvement.
